title.narrative: Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative: In April 2022, the Federation of Somali Trade Unions (FESTU) developed a national labour-poinered OSH policy to inform the domestication and implementation of ILO C155 and C187. Following the presentation of this policy to the Minister of Labour and Social Affairs (MOLSA), an ad hoc tripartite committee composed of 5 representatives of MOLSA, and 3 representatives each from employers (SCCI) and workers (FESTU) were appointed with the mandate to draft a national tripartite OSH policy using the draft labour-led national OSH policy as the main reference document. As a result, a draft National Tripartite OSH Policy was developed and has been submitted to the Federal Government of Somalia for endorsement. FESTU, in March 2022, advocated for scaling up of public funding for the health and livelihoods sector which specifically informed the design and launch of a cash transfer program, dubbed Baxnaano. FESTU also advocated for the adoption of the first generation of Somalia's Decent Work Country Program in June 2023, which, among other things, lays particular emphasis on inclusive growth strategies and improving working conditions and the well-being of Somali workforce through sound implementation of SDG 8. FESTU's constructive engagement in pursuing the revision of the Somali Labour Code informed its approval by the Cabinet and now awaits enactment by the Federal Parliament. In September 2022, FESTU developed an advocacy position paper on climate change, greening and transition just ahead of COP 27. The Government welcomed the priorities set by trade unions, in particular the commitment to just transition, the call for prioritization of investments in renewable energy and vocational training as well as the promotion of social dialogue as a tool to achieve these goals through an inclusive decision-making process. FESTU pushed for and played a constructive role that informed Somalia's recent enactment of a new environmental law that emphasized just transition. The ILO provided technical assistance and conducted several workshops for FESTU using Regular Budget for Technical Cooperation(RBTC) funds and resources from Development Cooperation Projects; including Better Regional Migration Project (BRMM) project, the Towards SDG Target 8.7 project and the US funding; the Labour-led National OSH Policy Validation Workshop; the Capacity Building on OSH for Somali Trade Unions; awareness-raising workshop on the importance of ratification of C138 to accelerate the elimination of child labour in Somalia; Capacity Building for Somalia Journalists Under Siege; Towards personal and professional safety through the effective domestication and application ILO OSH Conventions, and other capacity building activities.
